human_tolerance.notes: A habitat generalist that thrives in human-modified places: walls, rock gardens, paving, rubble and railway embankments. Introduced populations in the north-eastern United States, including New Jersey, live in gardens and along rail corridors.

phases.name: breeding
phases.note: 'The reproductive season of P. siculus begins in May and ends in July'; exact dates are from the source.

phases.name: dormancy
phases.note: As a temperate ectotherm it brumates through the coldest months; exact dates are a judgement.

taxonomy.note: Class Reptilia, order Squamata and family Lacertidae from ITIS; the GBIF backbone returns class Squamata with an empty order for this species, so ITIS is used for the hierarchy while GBIF supplies the usage key.

common_names.note: en label from Wikidata; fr/de labels are Wikidata sitelink-derived labels for Q1641251.

range.note: Native and introduced countries from the Distribution section: native to Italy, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Croatia, France, Montenegro, Serbia, Slovenia and Switzerland; introduced to Spain, Turkey, the United States and Canada. Spain is marked invasive per the article's account of it displacing the native Podarcis virescens.

traits.locomotion_modes.note: A ground-dwelling lacertid that runs and also climbs walls, rock faces and trees; Walk and Climb are listed.

traits.thermoregulation.note: A reptile; the article describes basking behaviour, especially by gravid females.

traits.nest_type.note: 'P. siculus is oviparous'; the eggs are laid in a shallow depression or burrow in the ground.

traits.mass_kg.note: Judgement: the article gives no mass; a small lacertid of 15-25 cm snout-vent length typically weighs about 6-16 g, so 10 g is used as a typical adult figure.

traits.mass_range_kg.note: Judgement: an approximate 6-16 g adult mass range for a lizard of this size.

traits.length_m.note: 'The snout-vent length of P. siculus is 150-250 mm'; adding a tail of roughly the same length again gives a total nose-to-tail-tip length of about 30 cm, used here.

traits.shoulder_height_m.note: Judgement: a low-bodied lizard about 2 cm at the shoulder.

traits.lifespan_y.note: Judgement: small lacertids typically live about 3-5 years in the wild; 4 years is used.

traits.home_range_ha.note: Judgement: a small, site-faithful territorial lizard with a home range on the order of a few hundred square metres.

traits.diet.note: 'P. siculus is a generalist predator. Its diet consists of a wide variety of invertebrates, mainly arthropods ... predates on small vertebrates as well. Plant matter comprises a much greater percentage of the diet of P. siculus than other related lizards.' Shares are a rounded judgement.

traits.social.note: Territorial and generally solitary outside the breeding season; group_size is judgement.

traits.activity_pattern.note: An ectotherm that basks and forages by day, especially in the morning; the article describes basking behaviour.

traits.defense.note: Dashes into cover when approached; like other lacertids it can also shed its tail.

traits.wariness.note: Judgement: a quick, wary lizard that flees at the first approach.

habitat.use.note: Judgement split: mostly on the ground and on low surfaces, with some climbing of walls, rocks and trees.

habitat.shelter_tag.note: Hides in crevices and holes in walls, rocks and the ground; 'cavity' is the closest tag.

habitat.resources.note: Food weights follow traits.diet; cavity, log_pile, shelter and water weights are qualitative.

habitat.human_tolerance.note: urban_affinity, uses_gardens and the notes follow 'P. siculus is a habitat generalist and can thrive in natural and human-modified environments' and its establishment in gardens and along rail corridors in the north-eastern United States.

seasonal.strategy.note: A temperate ectotherm, so it brumates in winter; the article does not use the word, but the species is inactive in the cold months. Enter/exit triggers are judgement.

seasonal.triggers.note: Authored: brumation begins after about five days below 10 C and ends after about five days above 12 C.

seasonal.phases.note: 'The reproductive season of P. siculus begins in May and ends in July'; the brumation window is a judgement.

seasonal.life_stages.note: 'Females can lay 3 or 4 clutches of 4-7 eggs per year'; incubation lasts several weeks and young reach maturity the following year. duration_days and scale are a judgement approximation.

look.note: Colours from the article: a green or brown back with a white or green belly and a long tail. The green morph is modelled. Proportions and extra-part placement are judgement.

behavior.note: Authored parameters for the shared ground-forager program: invertebrate-based foraging, a short flee distance for a small wary lizard, a walk gait, and rest while the sun is below the horizon (active by day).
